title: reg_code_blocks carries one count for both its size and its used entries, so a recursive compile writes into a reallocated array
live_proof: upstream fixed it in 40727c420c (40727c420c8e9ed61971dd46fc738132b9e4d5db) (2024-05-06). That commit is an ancestor of v5.45.3-85-gdb19522155 and is NOT an ancestor of the v5.36.3 tag (checked with git merge-base --is-ancestor, both directions), so it never reached the 5.36 maintenance branch; the pin's tree shows the unfixed code (pin regexp.h:94 int count (one field for both size and used); regcomp.c:7291 dst = &pRExC_state->code_blocks->cb[n] with n reset per recursion). Host ASan at the pin: ASan: SEGV (rc=77); the same trigger, same harness and same ASan options on master: no report (rc=0, the harness reports [PASS])
fidelity: the trigger is the test upstream added with its own fix, extracted onto a self-contained harness that collects failures instead of aborting, so one script yields one verdict. It is upstream's own reproduction, not a reduction of ours; what it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: SIGPROT: the defence reports; with revocation off (_RUNTIME_REVOCATION_DISABLE=1) the same binary gives: SIGPROT: the defence reports
cheribsd-revocation.verdict_note: also SIGPROT with revocation off, so bounds or another check fired, not revocation; no fixed-arm control has shown the fault is the defect

status: all three Capstone arms measured 2026-10-06 on the Capstone application VM, each after passing its own two controls; cheribsd-revocation measured 2026-10-06 on CheriBSD purecap, revocation selected per process because the system-wide default kills the guest's sshd, and every case run under both settings so the pair controls the knob (results/20261006-cheribsd)
allocator_layer: system allocator (the reg_code_block array, via Newx/Renew)
fault_sites_why: Host ASan at the pin (results/20261006-host-differential, the run of 2026-10-06 before any virtual run): SEGV, frames #0-#1 Perl_SvREFCNT_dec_NN | S_free_codeblocks (sites.tsv; the interpreter's dispatch loops Perl_runops_standard and Perl_yyparse are not sites).
class_correction: 2026-10-11: not a temporal defect. One count serves as both the array's size and its used entries, so S_free_codeblocks walks entries whose src_regex was never written and dereferences garbage. Host ASan at the pin reports a SEGV on a high-value address with its default fill of new memory (0xbe) and nothing at all with malloc_fill_byte=0, where the test gives the same five wrong results as on Capstone and CheriBSD (results/2026-10-11-virtual/case06-asan-fill.txt). ASan flags every read of freed or out-of-bounds memory, so no ended lifetime is involved: no lifetime protection can catch it, and it is outside the temporal denominators.
